idiom_name: delegate (Action/Func) + interface abstraction; reified generics instead of erasure
implementation_notes: C# needs no hand-written erasure wrapper for the common cases: a delegate instance (Action<...>/Func<...>, variant in their type parameters and generic for arbitrary signatures) already stores any matching method, lambda or method group behind one nominal type, and an interface reference stores any implementing type - including types from assemblies that share no base class. Generics are reified in .NET: a constructed generic type exists at runtime, keeps reflection support and does not box value types, so the storage problem that motivates erasure in C++ mostly does not arise. The escape hatch is dynamic (DLR call sites), which erases static checking instead of fixing it and should stay out of production APIs. Hand-roll the classic Concept/Model wrapper only for a non-generic public API that must hold an open set of types under a custom behaviour set.
code_sketch:
Action<LogEntry> sink = Console.WriteLine;                // method group binds
sink += entry => file.WriteLine(entry);                  // any lambda with that shape
IComparer<Order> byTotal =
    Comparer<Order>.Create((a, b) => a.Total.CompareTo(b.Total));  // interface over any comparer

object boxed = 42;                                       // fully erased: boxes the int
dynamic d = boxed;                                       // DLR: resolved at run time, unchecked
pitfalls: Delegate targets keep their target object alive: a long-lived publisher holding a delegate to a short-lived subscriber leaks the subscriber (unsubscribe with -= or use weak events).
Boxing: routing a value type through object, a non-generic interface or dynamic allocates; Action<T>/Func<...> or a generic interface keeps it unboxed.
dynamic defers every error to run time (a missing member throws at the call, not at compile), so an interface or delegate is the statically checked expression of the same intent.
